saurosuchus:research:1.title: 2026 in archosaur paleontology (research: General pseudosuchian research)

facts.statement: Saurosuchus lived during the Late Triassic period, specifically from the Late Carnian to the Early Norian stages.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Triassic, Late Carnian to Early Norian

facts.statement: The first Saurosuchus specimen was discovered in 1957 by Galileo J. Scaglia and Leocadio Soria in northwestern Argentina.
facts.quote: The first and holotype specimen was discovered in 1957 by Galileo J. Scaglia and Leocadio Soria in the strata of the Ischigualasto Formation in northwestern Argentina.

facts.statement: The species Saurosuchus galilei was formally named in 1959 by Osvaldo A. Reig.
facts.quote: The type and only species, S. galilei, was named in 1959 by Osvaldo A. Reig.

facts.statement: Adult Saurosuchus measured between 5.5 and 7 meters in length and weighed up to 590 kilograms.
facts.quote: Saurosuchus is estimated to have measured 5.5 - 7 m in length and to have weighed up to 590 kg

facts.statement: The skull of Saurosuchus could reach 58.6 cm in length and was strongly convergent with large theropod dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Its skull was large, measuring up to 58.6 cm, and was strongly convergent with that of large theropod dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Saurosuchus lived in floodplain and river environments that experienced seasonal rainfall.
facts.quote: Saurosuchus inhabited a region dominated by floodplains and fluvial environments, which would have experienced seasonal rainfall.

facts.statement: Saurosuchus was likely the apex predator of its Late Triassic environment.
facts.quote: It would probably have been the apex predator of its environment.

facts.statement: Analysis of the braincase suggests Saurosuchus had a high hearing range tuned to low frequencies and relied heavily on its sense of smell to find food.
facts.quote: Endocast analysis of Saurosuchus' braincase suggests that it had a high hearing range, though was most attuned to detecting low-frequency sounds, and that it was heavily reliant on its sense of smell to locate sources of food.

facts.statement: The name Saurosuchus comes from Greek words meaning 'lizard' and 'crocodile'.
facts.quote: The generic name, Saurosuchus, is derived from the Greek σαῦρος (sauros, meaning lizard) and σοῦχος (souchus, meaning crocodile).

facts.statement: The species name 'galilei' honors Galileo J. Scaglia, who discovered and prepared the holotype specimen.
facts.quote: The specific name, galilei, is in honour to Galileo J. Scaglia, who unearthed and prepared the holotype.

facts.statement: Adult Saurosuchus adults measured 5.5 to 7 meters long and weighed approximately 590 kg.
facts.quote: Adults measured between 5.5 - 7 m in length, and are estimated to have weighed 590 kg.

facts.statement: Sub-adult specimens of Saurosuchus are estimated to have been 4.07 meters long and weighed about 385 kg.
facts.quote: Two sub-adult specimens are estimated to have measured 4.07 m long and weighed approximately 385 kg.

facts.statement: The largest known skulls of Saurosuchus galilei measure approximately 58.6 cm in length.
facts.quote: The largest known S. galilei skulls, those of the holotype (PVL 2026) and PVSJ 32, are about the same length, 58.6 cm

facts.statement: The Saurosuchus skull was 17 cm wide at the back and narrowed to 10 cm in front of the eyes.
facts.quote: The skull is deep and somewhat compressed laterally (from side-to-side): it was wide at the back, measuring 17 cm at its widest extent, and narrows in front of the eyes, measuring 10 cm in front of the orbits (eye sockets).

facts.statement: Saurosuchus possessed large, recurved, and serrated teeth.
facts.quote: The teeth of S. galilei are large, recurved, and serrated.

facts.statement: Saurosuchus had two rows of leaf-shaped osteoderms running along the midline of its spine.
facts.quote: Two rows of osteoderms sit on the vertebral midline, one on each side.

facts.statement: Saurosuchus is now classified as a basal member of the clade Loricata, which includes rauisuchians and crocodylomorphs.
facts.quote: Saurosuchus was considered a member of the Rauisuchia, although the clade is now considered paraphyletic and Saurosuchus is considered a basal member of Loricata, a clade comprising "rauisuchians" as well as crocodylomorphs.

facts.statement: Recent analyses place Saurosuchus within the loricatan clade Prestosuchidae.
facts.quote: In more recent analyses, Saurosuchus has been found within the loricatan clade Prestosuchidae.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Saurosuchus fossils found in the Chinle Formation of Arizona belong to this species or to an indeterminate rauisuchian.
facts.quote: Saurosuchus was also reported from the Chinle Formation of Arizona in 2002 on the basis of isolated teeth and small skull fragments. The diagnostic value of these bones has been questioned in later studies, which considered them to be from an indeterminate species of rauisuchian.

facts.statement: Saurosuchus had a short, robust neck that was powerfully muscled.
facts.quote: Its neck was short and robust, and would have been powerfully muscled.

facts.statement: Saurosuchus likely had nine shortened and robust cervical vertebrae, creating a strong neck.
facts.quote: The cervical (neck) vertebrae of Saurosuchus, of which there were likely nine, are shortened and robust, and as such the neck would have been strong.

facts.statement: The Saurosuchus pelvic girdle featured an ischium split into two expansions, with the anterior portion being thinner than the posterior one.
facts.quote: The pelvic girdle (the hip region) is similar to that of other crurotarsans, with an ischium split into two large expansions: the anterior portion is thinner than the posterior one.

facts.statement: Saurosuchus was likely the largest member of its group, measuring about 7 meters in length, with the possible exception of the less known Fasolasuchus.
facts.quote: Con una longitud de 7 metros, seguramente fue el mayor miembro de su grupo, con la excepción quizás del menos conocido Fasolasuchus.

facts.statement: Like other rauisuchians, Saurosuchus walked on four fully extended legs.
facts.quote: Al igual que otros rauisuquios, Saurosuchus caminaba sobre cuatro patas completamente extendidas.

facts.statement: It is probable that Saurosuchus could stand up on its hind legs for short periods.
facts.quote: Es probable que fuera capaz de erguirse sobre las patas traseras por cortos períodos.

facts.statement: Saurosuchus had a deep skull that was compressed laterally.
facts.quote: Tenía un cráneo profundo y comprimido lateralmente.

facts.statement: Its teeth were large, recurved, and serrated.
facts.quote: Los dientes son grandes, recurvados y aserrados.

facts.statement: The cranial vault and maxilla possessed pits, a distinctive trait not seen in any other rauisuchian.
facts.quote: La bóveda craneana y el maxilar poseen hoyuelos, un rasgo distintivo no visto en ningún otro rauisuquio.

facts.statement: The frontal bone, located on top of the skull, was elongated to form thick ridges over the eyes.
facts.quote: El hueso frontal, localizado en la cima del cráneo, está alargado hasta formar unos gruesos rebordes sobre los ojos.

facts.statement: Some dorsal osteoderms ran along the back of Saurosuchus.
facts.quote: Algunos osteodermos dorsales corrían a lo largo de la espalda de Saurosuchus.

facts.statement: There were two rows of leaf-shaped osteoderms on each side of the midline, each strongly joined to the ones in front and behind.
facts.quote: De estos había dos filas a cada lado de la línea media, con cada osteodermo en forma de hoja uniéndose fuertemente con los de delante y los de detrás de estos.

facts.statement: A 2023 analysis estimated Saurosuchus had a surprisingly weak bite for its size, with forces of 1015 and 1885 N at the front and back of the jaws, comparable to modern gharials.
facts.quote: Analysis of the best preserved Saurosuchus specimen (PVSJ 32) performed by Fawcett and colleagues in 2023 indicated that it had a generally mechanically strong skull but a surprisingly weak bite for an animal of its size, with estimated bite forces of 1015 and 1885 N at the front and back of the jaws respectively, comparable to modern gharials.

facts.statement: Researchers argue Saurosuchus did not eat bone but instead defleshed carcasses by using its rear teeth to bite off or scrape muscle while avoiding bone contact.
facts.quote: Based on their analysis they argue that Saurosuchus did not possess adaptations for osteophagy, opting instead for a feeding behavior involving defleshing carcasses by biting off or scrapping muscle tissue with their teeth, as has been also inferred for the related Batrachotomus, different to Batrachotomus, however, which shows evidence for a preference in the use of the premaxillary teeth for defleshing with high tooth-bone interactions, Saurosuchus would have used its rear teeth and avoided contact with bone altogether.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests Saurosuchus relied on smell rather than eyesight to track prey and was not a particularly agile predator.
facts.quote: A reconstruction of the cranial endocast revealed large olfactory bulbs, poorly developed flocculus and optic lobes, and an anteroposteriorly short lateral semicircular canal, suggesting that Saurosuchus would have relied on smell instead of eyesight to track prey over long distances or at night, and that it would not have been a particularly agile predator.

facts.statement: A hypertrophied hypophysis in Saurosuchus may be correlated with its large size and rapid growth rates.
facts.quote: A hypertrophied hypophysis has also been reported for Saurosuchus, which may be correlated with large size and possibly rapid growth rates, as observed in the majority of other "rauisuchians" based on bone microstructure.

facts.statement: The environment where Saurosuchus lived was dominated by fluvial and floodplain areas with strongly seasonal rainfall.
facts.quote: The Ischigualasto Formation was dominated by fluvial and floodplain environments with strongly seasonal rainfalls.

facts.statement: Volcanic ash layers in the formation indicate Saurosuchus lived between approximately 231.4 and 227 million years ago.
facts.quote: Interlayered volcanic ash layers above the base and below the top of the formation provide chronostratigraphic control and have yielded ages of 231.4 ± 0.3 Ma and 227 ± 0.9 Ma respectively.

facts.statement: Saurosuchus lived in the Late Triassic in territories of modern-day Argentina.
facts.quote: Vivió en el Triásico Superior, en territorios de la actual Argentina.

facts.statement: Saurosuchus lived during the Carnian age, from 233.6 to 227.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (233.6 to 227.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus Saurosuchus was named by Reig in 1959.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Reig, 1959

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is S. galilei, named by Reig in 1959.
facts.quote: subdivision: S. galilei Reig, 1959 (tipo)

facts.statement: The type species S. galilei was named in 1959.
facts.quote: La especie tipo S. galilei fue nombrada en 1959.

facts.statement: It is debated whether isolated teeth and small cranial fragments found in the Chinle Formation of Arizona belong to Saurosuchus, as later studies consider them to be from an indeterminate rauisuchian species.
facts.quote: Saurosuchus fue también reportado en la formación Chinle de Arizona en 2002 sobre la base de dientes aislados y pequeños fragmentos craneales. El valor diagnóstico de estos huesos ha sido cuestionado en estudios posteriores, que los han considerado como de una especie indeterminada de rauisuquio.

rejected.statement: A 2026 study found Saurosuchus exhibited fibrolamellar bone complexes, suggesting it underwent rapid growth faster than any other sampled taxon except Sillosuchus.
rejected.quote: In 2026, a paper authored by Denis A. Ponce, Ignacio A. Cerda, and Julia B. Desojo examined bone growth patterns in various Late Triassic pseudosuchians from South America. They found that Saurosuchus exhibits fibrolamellar complexes (a kind of bone tissue found in fast-growing taxa, particularly as juveniles), which suggest that it underwent fairly rapid growth, faster than any other sampled taxon (barring Sillosuchus).
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'rapid growth faster than any other sampled taxon'

rejected.statement: Saurosuchus was likely the apex predator of its environment in the Cancha de Bochas Member of the Ischigualasto Formation.
rejected.quote: Saurosuchus was unearthed in the Cancha de Bochas Member from the Ischigualasto Formation, and was likely the apex predator of its environment.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'was likely the apex predator of its environment'
